page.layout: Two printed blocks on one page: running text in one column across the full width, with marginal notes in the left margin beside the Greek and Latin lines and a single side note in the left margin near the middle. Full-width heading "LX." and a title line above the text, then a block of text with a Greek and Latin verse quotation, then the running paragraphs. Marginal notes: left margin, three notes (Simulatio, ut vid., Imbecillitas). Final word "Nullæ" set large at the lower right.

main_text.head: LX. Sola mors nulla simulatione aut mi-nis abfterretur.
main_text.p: Quod apud Ariftophanem in Ranis Æfchylus: Μόνῳ θεῶν γὰρ ἢ Φυτάλῳ ἢ δώμων ἐχέ,
Mors sola donis nescit oblatis capi: honnihil à nobis immutatum dici recte queat: Πλαξὶν μόνῳ γὰρ ἢ Φυτάλῳ ὅτι ἔχει λόγων,

p.i: Mors sola verbis spernit argutis capi.

main_text.p: Quanquam hæc ita sint, tamen Tiberius, uti per ô-minem vitam simulationum techniis confutus, itâ etiam contrá mortem irruentem se simulatione ar-mavit. Jam Tiberium corpus, jam vires, nondum dis-simulatio deserebat. Idem animi rigor, sermone ac vultu intentus, quasi interdum comitate, quamvis manifestam defectionem tegebat. Sed biduo inter-mortuus, non potuit obitum ullos mortales celare; nec vitam reducem sæva in morte simulare. Aliis in rebus diu simulatio etiam perspicacissimos fallit: Fu-cus cadaverosæ faciei illitus, pro formidanda faciem splendentem oculis deceptis objicit. Vulpinam no-cendi astutiam multi blandimentis, & simulata amici-tiæ fronte obducunt. Hilaritatem in luctu, aut contrá luctum in hilaritate multi fingunt. Quæ creberrima fallendi materies, plurimi vitiorum fasciculis in finu abditis, proborum virorum externa larva vultum in-duunt. Etiam vires quis in defectione, visus acumen Simulatioexacutientibus oculis affimulare conatus est. Solam in morte vitam, in dissolutione animæ præsentiam; Imbecillitasnemo mortalium fingendo repræ-sentavit.

page.notes: Nearly all Greek is badly worn; the Greek verse lines are copied as best read and may contain errors. The left-margin notes are partly cut and read from the scan: "Simulatio" with "ut vid.", and "Imbecillitas", placed beside the paragraph. The faint lines in the lower left and the bottom right are show-through from the other side and are left out. The word "Nullæ" at the foot is a large printed catchword-like line and is not included in the text; it may belong to the next section.
